authors: Gao, H., Tang, Y., Jing, L., Li, H. & Ding, H.
title: A novel unsupervised segmentation quality evaluation method for remote sensing images
relevance: The remote-sensing tradition of unsupervised segmentation quality evaluation, scoring segments by spatial stratified heterogeneity and spatial autocorrelation with no ground truth. Include it to mark a DISTINCTION we must not blur: this measures whether segments are well FORMED (homogeneous inside, distinct from neighbours), not whether the label 'tree' is CORRECT. It could tell us a crown boundary is clean while the crown is actually a hedge. Useful as a geometry QC layer on the instance stream, and useless as an accuracy substitute - which is precisely the confusion an eager reading of ground-truth-free evaluation invites.

authors: Costa, H., Foody, G.M. & Boyd, D.S.
title: Supervised methods of image segmentation accuracy assessment in land cover mapping
relevance: Reviews how segmentation accuracy is properly assessed against reference data in land cover mapping, and separates geometric agreement from thematic correctness - the two things our per-crown deliverable must report separately and currently does not. Relevant because our crowns are evaluated as a binary canopy mask, so a crown that is correctly detected but badly delineated scores the same as one delineated perfectly, and the per-crown validity interval inherits that blindness. Sets the vocabulary for stating which kind of accuracy each of our numbers actually describes.
